strings.name: Marc Márquez
strings.summary: Márquez began racing as a child and won world titles in 125cc, Moto2 and MotoGP. A premier-class champion as a rookie in 2013, he spent many years with Honda. A severe 2020 injury and repeated operations redirected his career. After moving to Ducati machinery, he won again in 2025, completing a major recovery of his competitive form. His 2026 title defence remained unresolved at the cutoff.

strings.highlights.h1.title: Champion across classes
strings.highlights.h1.text: Won world championships in the 125cc, Moto2 and MotoGP categories.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Return after injury
strings.highlights.h2.text: Won on Ducati in 2025 after a fractured right arm and repeated operations.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Continued the 2026 title defence
strings.timeline.t1.text: Returned after mid-season foot-fracture surgery; second in Qatar left him 60 points ahead with two rounds remaining and the title undecided.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Seventh MotoGP crown
strings.timeline.t2.text: Clinched the title in Japan: his ninth world championship and seventh in the premier class.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Joined Gresini
strings.timeline.t3.text: Left Honda and rebuilt his competitiveness on Gresini's Ducati.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Fractured his right arm
strings.timeline.t4.text: A Jerez crash broke his humerus, leading to prolonged rehabilitation and further surgery.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Rookie champion
strings.timeline.t5.text: Won the riders' title for Honda in his first MotoGP season, becoming its youngest champion.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Won Moto2
strings.timeline.t6.text: Secured the intermediate-class title before advancing to MotoGP.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Won the 125cc title
strings.timeline.t7.text: Earned his first world championship, establishing his promise as a young racer.
strings.timeline.t8.title: World championship debut
strings.timeline.t8.text: Entered the 125cc world championship after developing in junior competitions.
